findings.highlight: their disposition toward Yanagihara-san's personality
findings.evidenceJa: 柳原朋の、元々の性格に起因するものだったり
findings.explanation: The gap in how quickly the friends understand is attributed partly to Tomo Yanagihara's own original personality. The English instead invents a disposition that the others have toward her personality.
findings.japanese:
それは、俺と過ごした時間の差だったり、
柳原朋の、元々の性格に起因するものだったり、
そんな様々な要因が絡んでのことだと思うけど…
findings.todokanai: It may be due to the difference in time spent with me, or merely their disposition toward Yanagihara-san's personality…

findings.highlight: improvise an answer
findings.evidenceJa: もし俺が口から出任せを言っても
findings.explanation: 口から出任せ means making up a convenient lie on the spot, not merely improvising an answer. This begins Haruki's imagined attempt to deceive his friends about the breakup.
findings.japanese: 今、もし俺が口から出任せを言っても…
findings.todokanai: Let's say I were to improvise an answer…

findings.highlight: we got into a little fight
findings.evidenceJa: 悪い、ちょっとやっちゃってさ
findings.explanation: Haruki's hypothetical lie remains deliberately vague: roughly, 'Sorry, I kind of screwed up.' The English specifies a fight, supplying a concrete explanation the source withholds.
findings.japanese:
『悪い、ちょっとやっちゃってさ…』なんて、
頭を掻きながら白々しく反省の表情を見せたとしても…
findings.todokanai: Scratch my head with a half regretful look on my face, and say "Sorry, we got into a little fight."

findings.highlight: Neither Takeya nor Io tried reinterpreting it to make me look better, even though I'm sure they could.
findings.evidenceJa: すぐに思いつきながらも、必死で思い描こうとしなかった最悪の事実
findings.explanation: Takeya and Io immediately thought of the worst possibility but had desperately resisted picturing it. The English replaces that denial with a nonexistent opportunity to reinterpret Haruki's confession favorably.
findings.japanese:
武也と依緒が、すぐに思いつきながらも、
必死で思い描こうとしなかった最悪の事実が、
俺の口から語られてしまったから。
findings.todokanai: I told the truth in its terrible entirety. Neither Takeya nor Io tried reinterpreting it to make me look better, even though I'm sure they could.

findings.highlight: and looks at Takeya and Io from the side
findings.evidenceJa: 柳原朋は俺を睨みつけ、武也は依緒の横顔を見つめ
findings.explanation: Tomo glares at Haruki, while Takeya looks at Io's profile. The English makes Tomo perform both actions and turns Io's profile into a side view of both Takeya and Io.
findings.japanese:
柳原朋は俺を睨みつけ、
武也は依緒の横顔を見つめ。
findings.todokanai: Yanagihara Tomo glares at me, and looks at Takeya and Io from the side.

findings.highlight: the true lie had been everything I had told her up until today
findings.evidenceJa: 今までの俺が嘘をついていたこと
findings.explanation: Tomo finally believes that Haruki had been lying or maintaining a lie until now. The English says everything he had ever told her was a lie, a much broader and materially different accusation.
findings.japanese:
今の俺が嘘をついていないって…
今までの俺が嘘をついていたことを、やっと信じた。
findings.todokanai: She finally understood that I'm not lying… That the true lie had been everything I had told her up until today.

findings.highlight: She desired the artist SETSUNA more than the actual Ogiso Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜が、小木曽雪菜であるよりも、ＳＥＴＳＵＮＡである時間をもっと求めてた
findings.explanation: Tomo wanted Setsuna to spend more time being the performer SETSUNA than being ordinary Ogiso Setsuna. The English instead says that Setsuna herself desired the stage persona more than the real person, reversing both subject and motivation.
findings.japanese:
雪菜が、小木曽雪菜であるよりも、
ＳＥＴＳＵＮＡである時間をもっと求めてた。
findings.todokanai: She desired the artist SETSUNA more than the actual Ogiso Setsuna.

findings.highlight: Did she find all your weak spots?
findings.evidenceJa: 身体の相性、抜群だった？
findings.explanation: Tomo asks whether Haruki and Kazusa were exceptionally sexually compatible. 'Find all your weak spots' is a different sexual idea and loses the comparison of bodily compatibility.
findings.japanese:
「そんなに彼女は良かった？
身体の相性、抜群だった？」
findings.todokanai: "Was she that good in bed? Did she find all your weak spots?"

findings.highlight: What a poor excuse for love.
findings.evidenceJa: 最低の純愛だね
findings.explanation: Tomo calls it 'the worst kind of pure love,' a pointed oxymoron that concedes the purity of Haruki and Kazusa's devotion while condemning its effects. 'Poor excuse for love' denies that central paradox.
findings.japanese: 「最低の純愛だね。吐き気がする」
findings.todokanai: "What a poor excuse for love. I feel like vomiting."

findings.highlight: my love for her isn't reaching them
findings.evidenceJa: 本当の心が通じないのが痛い。相手を好きな気持ちがもう二度と伝わらないのが痛い
findings.explanation: The narration describes the pain of two true hearts no longer communicating and one's love for the other never being conveyed again. The English collapses this into Haruki's unilateral feelings and ends with an incoherent her/them referent.
findings.japanese:
本当の心が通じないのが痛い。
相手を好きな気持ちがもう二度と伝わらないのが痛い。
findings.todokanai: It hurts that my feelings aren't being conveyed. It hurts that my love for her isn't reaching them.

findings.highlight: this is what Setsuna looks like after being abandoned by you
findings.evidenceJa: あんたに捨てられた雪菜はこんなもんじゃ
findings.explanation: Io says that what Setsuna suffered after Haruki abandoned her was nothing like this—implicitly far worse. The English instead identifies the present scene as what abandoned Setsuna looks like.
findings.japanese:
「でもな、春希…
雪菜は…あんたに捨てられた雪菜はこんなもんじゃ…」
findings.todokanai: "But you know, Haruki… this is what Setsuna looks like after being abandoned by you…"

findings.highlight: retribution for switching partners overnight
findings.evidenceJa: ただ、日を変え相手を変え、俺に返ってきた報い
findings.explanation: The same cruelty has returned to Haruki on another day and from another person: Io is now confronting him as he once confronted Setsuna. The English invents Haruki switching romantic partners overnight.
findings.japanese:
ただ、日を変え相手を変え、
俺に返ってきた報い。
findings.todokanai: This is my retribution for switching partners overnight.

findings.highlight: take on the responsibility for all my actions
findings.evidenceJa: いつもは俺がやってたことを、これからは自分の役目だと覚悟した
findings.explanation: Takeya appears resolved to take over the role Haruki had always played: shouldering responsibility for failing to persuade someone. The English vastly broadens this into responsibility for all of Haruki's actions.
findings.japanese:
それはまるで、いつもは俺がやってたことを、
これからは自分の役目だと覚悟したかのようで…
findings.todokanai: It's almost as though he's ready to take on the responsibility for all my actions…

findings.highlight: feeling cold because of the loneliness
findings.evidenceJa: そんな寒さが、俺の孤独感を呼び覚ましたのか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether the cold awakened his loneliness. The English reverses the causal direction and makes loneliness the cause of his feeling cold.
findings.japanese:
そんな寒さが、俺の孤独感を呼び覚ましたのか、
それとも他の理由なのかはわからないけど。
findings.todokanai: I'm not sure if I'm feeling cold because of the loneliness that's welling up within me, or if it's because of another reason.

findings.highlight: That's pretty under wraps.
findings.evidenceJa: なんつ～灯台の真下だよ。マスコミ全然気づいてないじゃん
findings.explanation: Takeya riffs on 灯台下暗し: Youko was hidden in plain sight, right under the media's nose. 'Under wraps' implies deliberate secrecy and loses the joke linking her location to the blind spot beneath a lighthouse.
findings.japanese:
「峰城大病院って…なんつ～灯台の真下だよ。
マスコミ全然気づいてないじゃん」
findings.todokanai: "Houjou University Hospital… That's pretty under wraps. The mass media doesn't know a thing, huh?"

findings.highlight: I might be unable to pick Kazusa anymore.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はもう、二人のうちからかずさを選べなくなる
findings.explanation: Haruki says that sharing the burden among all three would leave him no longer able to choose Kazusa over Setsuna. This is the categorical selfish motive for rejecting the proposed solution; 'might' improperly hedges it.
findings.japanese:
「………もし三人で背負ったら、
俺はもう、二人のうちからかずさを選べなくなる」
findings.todokanai: "…If we shared the burden among the three of us, then… I might be unable to pick Kazusa anymore."

findings.highlight: until I started believing them myself
findings.evidenceJa: 二年間、自分でも気づかないうちに嘘を重ねてたんだ
findings.explanation: Haruki says he had unknowingly piled up lies for two years. The English invents a progression in which he eventually came to believe those lies himself.
findings.japanese:
「二年前、吹っ切ったと思ってたけど違ってた。
ずっと昔から、何も変わってなかった。
二年間、自分でも気づかないうちに嘘を重ねてたんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I thought I was over her two years ago, but I was wrong. Even after all this time, nothing has changed. I only piled up lie over lie for these two years until I started believing them myself."

findings.highlight: I may not have any desire to be
findings.evidenceJa: 望みがないってわかってるけど、それでも、まだお前の親友だからさ
findings.explanation: Takeya knows there is no hope of changing Haruki's mind, but pleads because he is still Haruki's best friend. The English says Takeya may have no desire to remain his friend, reversing the force of his last appeal.
findings.japanese:
「けど俺、お前の親友だから。
望みがないってわかってるけど、
それでも、まだお前の親友だからさ…」
findings.todokanai: "But I'm still your friend. I may not have any desire to be, but even then, I'm still your friend…"

findings.highlight: I'll probably never be able to see him again
findings.evidenceJa: もう、二度と出会えないかもしれない存在
findings.explanation: Takeya was a singular kind of person Haruki might never encounter again, not merely someone he might never physically see again after this rupture. The English turns irreplaceability into future access.
findings.japanese:
俺にとって、唯一の…
もう、二度と出会えないかもしれない存在、だったんだ…
findings.todokanai: The only one I had… and I'll probably never be able to see him again…

findings.highlight: nostalgia that I once shared with him are brought to my mind
findings.evidenceJa: 新しい発見は、嬉しさと、悔しさと、切なさと。そして、懐かしさを俺の心に運んでくれる
findings.explanation: The new realization brings Haruki happiness, regret, heartache, and nostalgia. The English grammatically recasts the feelings as things Haruki once shared with Takeya, then makes them the subject of an incoherent sentence.
findings.japanese:
新しい発見は、嬉しさと、悔しさと、切なさと。
そして、懐かしさを俺の心に運んでくれる。
findings.todokanai: New discoveries, happiness, frustration, pain, and nostalgia that I once shared with him are brought to my mind.

findings.highlight: overwhelmed by all the things that had happened up until now
findings.evidenceJa: 今までこらえていたものが溢れそうになり
findings.explanation: What Haruki has been holding back—his tears or emotion—threatens to overflow when the crowd brings relief. The English substitutes the external events that happened, breaking the physical-emotional sequence that makes him look upward.
findings.japanese:
そんな、駅前の人の群れにほっとしてしまったのか、
今までこらえていたものが溢れそうになり、
思わず空を見上げるしかなくなる。
findings.todokanai: Perhaps I felt relieved by seeing the big crowd of people in front of the station, or perhaps I felt overwhelmed by all the things that had happened up until now, and before I knew it, I was looking up at the sky.

findings.highlight: the center of all my relationship problems
findings.evidenceJa: いつも、俺の人間関係の中心にいやがった
findings.explanation: Takeya was always at the center of Haruki's human relationships or social world. The source does not call those relationships problems; the insertion makes Takeya sound like their cause.
findings.japanese:
付属に入って、一番最初にできた友達だった。
いつも、俺の人間関係の中心にいやがった。
findings.todokanai: He was the first friend I ever made after I enrolled in high school. He was always at the center of all my relationship problems.
